title: Supermirrors meet the burn at the wrong angle
mechanism: X-ray mirrors reflect only at grazing angles of a few mrad; the burn-facing faces of the compact engine meet its rays at a median 54 deg
required: Reflected share of the X-rays on hardware that matters for heat (at least 0.5)
achieved: 1.5e-05 of the X-rays that strike (46 MW of 3.05 TW)
solutions: Edge-on structure (B) instead of coated faces; mirrors only where a surface can be made to contain the burn point
advances: None for hard X-rays: the critical angle is a property of matter (about 1/E)
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: No grazing deflector can steer the spectrum clear of a coil
mechanism: Clearing a coil needs a turn of about its angular width (0.09-0.26 rad); a grazing mirror turns a ray by at most twice the critical angle (Pt 68 mrad at 1 keV)
required: A deflection of 0.1-0.26 rad inside the 11.5 m engine envelope
achieved: Only photons below about 0.1 keV; none in the R2-B spectrum (1-1000 keV)
solutions: Remote geometry (MPN candidate F, RON B) where coils subtend milliradians
advances: Not reachable with reflection; geometry only
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Mirror coatings do not survive the pulse
mechanism: Each pulse puts up to 3.4 MJ/m2 of X-rays on the armour in about 10 ps; a 0.5 nm mirror finish ablates on the first pulse; neutron and helium damage roughen it further
required: Roughness below 1 nm for 10^7 pulses per hour
achieved: Ablation every pulse (tungsten surface jump about 10^5 K)
solutions: None for a mirror face; sacrificial low-Z faces renewed in service
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Armour shoes cover only part of each coil
mechanism: The drawn shoes (0.22 m section) shadow 37% of the cryostat silhouette the burn sees; the rest strikes the bare vessel
required: Full silhouette armour
achieved: 1.80 TW on bare cryostat vessels and joints (no coolant drawn there)
solutions: Strategy C layered blankets (2,147 t per engine with neutron layers, 248 t without)
advances: Lighter neutron shielding (hydrides, boron carbide composites)
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: No face material survives the X-ray pulse at 1800 K
mechanism: The pulse is far shorter than conduction: the surface layer takes the X-rays at once
required: Surface below melting or sublimation
achieved: Best is carbon: jump 2,866 K, margin -766 K; tungsten jumps 1.7e+05 K; Be and LiH survive the pulse but melt below the 1800 K loop
solutions: Low-Z sacrificial faces (carbon) at a colder loop; larger standoff (fluence falls as 1/d^2)
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Heat flux far above any coolant channel
mechanism: Lithium-cooled tungsten carries about 20 MW/m2 steady
required: Below 20 MW/m2 on every hot face
achieved: 96-1,250 times the limit; the armour channels would need lithium at 7-28 km/s
solutions: Spread the heat (standoff, larger faces); reduce the engine's sky share
advances: None in the channel: the flux is set by geometry
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Drawn lithium lines are far too small
mechanism: The supply feeder (r 0.11 m) and panel lines (r 0.12 m) carry lithium at most 10 m/s with a 300 K rise
required: 5.82 TW (all engine heat); 2.7 GW even at the canon radiator share
achieved: 216 MW: 27,013 times short; the budget alone needs 0.48 m2 of flow area
solutions: Lines sized for the budget (several 0.2-0.3 m mains); the full heat would need a 18 m pipe
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Liquid-metal MHD pressure loss in the coil field
mechanism: Lithium crossing 1-2.4 T near the windings induces currents that drag the flow (dp ~ sigma v B^2 L c)
required: Below the 1 MPa design pressure
achieved: 2.2-48 MPa per armour run at 10 m/s with bare walls; 0.09-2.0 MPa with SiC inserts
solutions: SiC flow-channel inserts; runs along the field; helium or molten salt in the strongest field
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Cryogenic refrigeration demand
mechanism: Neutrons reach the 20 K windings through the bare vessels; each watt there costs 297 W of refrigerator input
required: Refrigeration within the engine's power budget (MW class)
achieved: 25.2 GW at 20 K -> 7.46 TW of input; with blankets C 1.3 GW -> 394.4 GW
solutions: Thick neutron shields on every coil; warmer superconductors (40-77 K REBCO)
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Hot radiator area and mass
mechanism: Everything absorbed leaves by radiation at 1800 K
required: 2.7 GW per engine (canon share)
achieved: 1.09e+07 m2 per engine (404 times the ship's radiators, about 109 kt); Brayton recovery raises it 10-fold
solutions: Cut absorbed heat first; recovery runs the driver but enlarges the radiator
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: Thermal fatigue at the pulse rate
mechanism: Every face is heated and relaxed at the pulse rate
required: Fatigue life of a renewable face over one service interval
achieved: 2.1e+07 cycles per hour; one burn of days is 10^9-10^10 cycles
solutions: Faces renewed between burns (exchange units)
advances: OPEN: no fatigue data at these cycle counts
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: Hot and cryogenic circuits share a narrow gap
mechanism: The 1800 K armour shoe sits 0.16 m from the cryostat; radiation across the gap and the vessels' own heat need a warm stage
required: Separate hot, warm and cold circuits with no shared wall
achieved: 3.55 TW lands on warm parts drawn without a coolant; gap radiation about 4.1 MW per engine
solutions: A third (warm, about 300-600 K) circuit for vessels, cage and optics; polished screens in the gap
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: Edge-on structure needs sub-milliradian alignment
mechanism: A blade works only while its plane contains the burn point to about 0.11 mrad (source wander over distance); thermal growth and coil forces move the cage by millimetres
required: Alignment held to 0.1-1 mrad through each burn
achieved: Budget 0.13 mrad (target miss, mount, 1 K thermal bow, vibration); a 3.3 K face-to-face difference alone uses the whole allowance; first mode 35 Hz against 5,697 Hz pulses
solutions: Both faces cooled together, active root trim from the edge temperature map, constrained-layer dampers, cones instead of flat hoops
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
next: Continue under the owner's 2026-11-24 direction (B adopted, thin blanket optional, source first)

title: Driver final optics see the burn

required: Optics behind a shutter or a grazing turning mirror
achieved: 31.4 GW on 1.9 m2 of optics
solutions: Grazing metal turning mirrors (the one place a grazing mirror fits), fast shutters

title: Lithium leak or loss of flow in a magnet
mechanism: Lithium runs beside the cryostats; a leak shorts or attacks the vessel, a loss of flow lets the faces melt within milliseconds
required: Detection and isolation faster than the face heats
achieved: OPEN: no failure analysis
solutions: Double-walled runs, segment isolation valves, burn abort
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: Engine pickup undercounted in the ledger
mechanism: The compact sky ledger counted coils, shield and loops; the cage hoops, seats, struts and lines also see the burn
required: One sky trace for every drawn part
achieved: Trace 63.1% vs the compact study's piped share 54.6% (x1.16)
solutions: Audited 2026-11-24: the 54.6 % was a piped-heat residual from the steady source, not a geometric share; the coupled ledger now uses the trace
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: Edge-on blades concentrate the heat on their edges
mechanism: A blade aligned with the burn shows it only its edge, so the edge takes the full X-ray flux at its distance
required: Edge flux below the 20 MW/m2 a lithium-cooled face can take
achieved: 7.4 GW/m2 steady (372x), 1,102 K per pulse, 63% of CFC strength each pulse
solutions: Sacrificial replaceable edge strips on lithium-cooled roots (drawn), exchange ports at the aft hoop (drawn)
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: The target is its own X-ray lamp
mechanism: At the design density the 14.7 MeV protons stop within microns and give about 90 % of their energy to electrons, which radiate
required: X-ray share low enough that cooling can follow
achieved: 85% of the fusion energy as X-rays; hot ions, polarisation and 3He-rich fuel barely change it
solutions: Lower areal density, earlier extraction of the protons, an X-ray trapping tamper
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py

title: Energy taken from the X-rays strikes the nozzle instead
mechanism: Every lever that keeps energy in the plasma feeds the nozzle, and the compact nozzle puts about two thirds of the plasma on hardware
required: Hit share well below 0.1
achieved: Best source case: X-rays 23%, thrust x2.1, engine heat still x2,011 its radiator share (78% from strikes)
solutions: A nozzle with a small hit share (C3/C4 field, remote geometry)
assumptions: Coupled pulse, R2-B spectrum, drawn C1 engine, PROTOTYPE limits in thermal.py and source.py
